q: What is the first step of CompTIA's troubleshooting methodology?
opts: Establish a theory of probable cause

q: What should a technician do if a theory is disproved?
opts: Establish a new theory or escalate

q: A link shows climbing CRC errors. What is the most likely cause?
Late collisions on a switch port usually indicate what?
A new access point powers on and off repeatedly. What should be checked?
opts: The switch's PoE budget and the AP's power class

q: A workstation has a 169.254.x.x address. What is the most likely cause?
opts: The DHCP server cannot be reached

q: Users can ping servers by IP but not by name. What is the problem?
New devices stop getting addresses late in the day, but existing ones work. What is likely?
A host on the correct subnet cannot reach anything on its switch, while its neighbor can. What should be checked first?
opts: The VLAN assigned to its port

q: Which describes variation in packet delay that degrades voice calls?
Users in one area drop Wi-Fi when walking between rooms. What is the likely issue?
Two nearby APs on channel 6 cause slow Wi-Fi. What is the problem?
Which tool finds which hop along the path is failing?
Which command shows IP-to-MAC mappings on a host?
Which tool captures and decodes packets on the wire?
